Great little washer, but time consuming. - This was a great little washer. It has a very powerful motor for washing. Does a great job at getting out all the dirt and filth. The water pump worked worked great. It usually got almost all the water out, I'd just have to tilt it a little at the very end. I would highly recommend that you leave the drain hose on the floor (or even bellow) to a drain the washer. The pump does not pump against gravity very well and water stays behind in the hose and lower reservoirs. The spinner section also works great. It spins really fast and does an awesome job at removing lots of water from the clothes. They always came out slightly damp, but never soaking wet. They would air dry within a day. Watch the balance carefully, if unbalanced the spinner rotates violently and shakes the machine, making a lot of noise. I usually wash in the tub, so as to avoid cleaning excess spills and keep drain below the level of the washer. Something that I didn't like and why I only gave 4 stars. It requires a lot of attention. You need to move the clothes ever to change the water/rinse every 15/20 min. Then spin and rinse some more, back for another quick wash, and rinse/spin again. It takes some effort. The water hose does not work very well. I usually use the detachable shower head to fill and rinse. Lastly, I felt like the load size for the spinner was small compared to washer, could only do small loads at a time. It came well packed and in good condition.

Made in China. Know what to expect before purchasing. - I’ve used several similar ice machines. There are several things you need to know before you purchase this machine to make sure your expectations meet exactly what this machine offers.

First of all, this machine is not connected to water. You fill the reservoir, in the front. Once the water is low, you refill the reservoir.

The listing shows that this machine can make 33# of ice in a 24-hour period. That is only possible if you have someone removing the ice from the basket . . . 24-hous. . . day-and-night.

This machine does not keep the ice frozen. The ice empties into a basket in the front. If you do not remove the ice; it will melt and refreeze. If you want to keep the ice frozen, you must remove it from the basket. . . place it into a plastic bag or container. . .and place it into your freezer. Note that the ice will be “wet” so when you remove it from the freezer, you’ll need to break it apart.

You should turn the machine off when not in use. Such as nights. Otherwise the machine will continue to make ice. . . the ice melts. . . and recycles making ice again and again.

When you clean the machine, you need to add some coffee machine cleaner powder (the type which is mostly citric acid). I use a bottle brush to clean the inside the best that I can. When you start the cleaning cycle, it will run the solution through the machine several times. You need to make sure you use fresh clean water and let it cycle a few times also.

This ice machine is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. This machine makes 24 small cubes at a time. Other, similar machines, are offered which make nice cubes for under a hundred bucks. Some also have a timer so they turn-off at night.

Well Engineered & Good Output - It took a bit of trial and error, but, I got the machine working well. Instructions could have been a lot clearer.
Water is poured into a reservoir that holds about 1 1/2 liters. The machine produces a "rack" of ice about every 15 minutes. Four cycles will fill the catch box holding the ice. This needs to be emptied after 20 minutes or so since the ice will begin to melt as if it were in a refrigerator. The melt drains off and recycles through the machine so it is not a problem if one doesn't mind smaller ice cubes; they are small to begin with.

The machine works by water flowing from a horizontal tube with many very small holes that allow water to flow over the ice-making rack. It is obvious that the water put into the reservoir must be scrupulously clean. I currently use only filtered water. I think this is essential to prevent a breakdown.

The size of the cubes does vary and can be adjusted. Some people put the fresh ice into bags before putting the ice in a freezer. This is helpful since the fresh ice will "clot" and need to be separated somewhat. I use a wood mallet for the purpose. If the ice is placed into a plastic bag just dropping it on a counter should work to separate the ice.

The making of ice is quite noisy. If I am in the same room as the machine, it sounds like a truck going by.

I am impressed so far. Fridgedaire put a lot of thought into the machine. Cheaper versions of ice-makers have a high rate of negative reviews while Fridigaire has good reviews overall. You will pay for that— It's worth it.
